absent: Locking or concurrency rules for debug registers, register cache bitmaps and SMM state are not shown.
Validity predicates for debug status and control and refresh behavior of breakpoint helpers are not shown.
Event-request, triple-fault, EOI-map and MMU-reset effects beyond being requested are not shown.
Segment-selector values, descriptor-table accessors and interrupt-shadow encoding are not shown.
Full numeric values of reserved-bit complements and complete reverse-CPUID table entries are not enumerated here.
Log prefix and header-guard mechanics carry no behavioral contract beyond naming.

findings.text: Query operation for guest debug registers refuses protected guests, applies an exception-payload compatibility adjustment, clears the caller buffer, copies breakpoint address slots from per-vCPU storage, and returns status plus control values with success on the normal path.

Update operation for guest debug registers refuses protected guests, requires zero caller flags, validates proposed status and control values with dedicated helpers, stores breakpoint slots, refreshes derived breakpoint state, records new status and control, then refreshes control-derived state.

Guest-ownable control subsets and reload groupings are fixed. First control allows task-switch and write-protect indications. Second control allows nine flags for interrupt virtualization, debugging, counting, floating-point, paging, access control and base management. Companion groupings combine cache-disable, paging and protection bits for pointer reload and flush decisions.

Reserved masks for the first two control registers are the bitwise complement of their architecturally valid bits, so any outside bit is reserved. The eighth control mask permits only the task-priority field.

Debug status positions are fixed: bus-lock at bit 11, debug-access at 13, single-step at 14, task-switch at 15, transactional-memory at 16. Control positions are global-enable at 9 and debug-access at 13. Mask facts: active-low ffff0ff0, volatile 1e80f, low-byte breakpoint-enable ff, control volatile ffff2bff, with a fixed-one mask derived from active-low minus volatile.

General-register helpers share one per-vCPU array slot per architectural index. Full read applies a mode-dependent mask, raw read returns stored width unchanged, raw write replaces it, and the narrow pair exchanges only the low 32 bits through the same slot.

Register caching uses availability and dirty bitmaps guarded by a common precondition. Dirty query tests one bit, mark-for-reload clears both bits for that index, mark-available sets availability, and test-and-mark atomically sets availability while reporting its prior state.

Bulk cache maintenance assumes single-word bitmaps. Availability clearing uses AND with the inverted caller mask so eagerly synchronized entries cannot silently become unavailable, while dirty reset writes zero to the whole dirty word.
Page-size-extension status is determined by testing the corresponding bit in the guest view of the fourth control register.
Guest-mode tracking pairs a hidden-flags bit with a statistics counter. Entry sets both. Exit clears the flag, drains a pending EOI-exit-map load by raising its request, then clears the counter.

Feature identifiers encode a CPUID word index scaled by 32 plus a bit number. Fixed assignments cover enclave leaves, MSR behavior, vector and matrix extensions, speculation controls, accelerator aliases, vector-length variants, constant timestamp, performance-monitor version and store-safety indicators.

Reverse lookup uses a descriptor holding leaf, subleaf and register selector plus a table indexed by internal word identifier. Each entry names the CPUID function and output register backing that word across standard, extended and hypervisor-specific leaves.
Per-entry feature updates resolve the backing 32-bit register for a feature identifier and then clear or set only that feature bit, leaving sibling bits unchanged.

32-bit management save image is 512 bytes with offsets validated relative to FE00. Anchors include general registers at FFD0, debug control at FFC8, debug status at FFCC, instruction pointer at FFF0, flags at FFF4, third control at FFF8, first control at FFFC, base at FEF8 and revision at FEFC, with segments, tables, restart hints and shadow state at fixed positions between.

64-bit management save image is 512 bytes with offsets validated relative to FE00. Anchors include segments from FE00 upward, revision at FEFC, base at FF00, shadow-stack pointer at FF18, first control at FF58, third control at FF50, fourth control at FF48, debug control at FF60, debug status at FF68, flags at FF70, instruction pointer at FF78 and general registers at FF80, plus feature, virtualization and restart fields at fixed positions.

Management-mode transitions update hidden flags and address context. Entry sets the SMM indicator. Exit clears SMM and inside-NMI indicators, raises an event request for latched input, clears the userspace-loaded pointer flag so pointers reload from guest memory, and resets translation context in both directions.

Incoming management interrupt handling only latches a pending flag and raises an event request for later delivery. Segment saving reads the live guest segment and records selector, base, limit and a flag word assembled from granularity, size, mode, availability, presence, privilege and type attributes, with 64-bit form storing selector alongside and shifting the flag word.

32-bit entry snapshot captures control state, flags, instruction pointer, eight general registers, debug status and control, all segment states and selectors, global and interrupt tables, revision 00020000, current base and interrupt-shadow state.

64-bit entry snapshot captures sixteen general registers in reversed slot order, instruction pointer, flags, debug and control registers, base, revision 00020064, extended feature register, segment states, descriptor tables, interrupt-shadow state, and shadow-stack pointer when the guest advertises that capability.

Invalid debug-register proposals are rejected without partial update, protected guests are rejected for both query and update, and a failed shadow-stack read during 64-bit management entry requests triple fault instead of continuing with stale state.
